For online learning, we can expect some domain knowledge for the first tasks, but it is unrealistic to assume knowledge of the safe states for all the future tasks, especially in an infinite MDP. It would be helpful to have a mechanism able to predict safe states for unseen tasks based on the context or on task similarities. The algorithms we discussed provide a wide range of approaches to ensure online learning safety. This section summarizes proposed solutions across the following five areas: learning, adaptation, optimization, safety consideration, and the type of environment (see Table 1 and Table 2 ). We also provide details on the theoretical foundation of the algorithms, including the main assumptions of the algorithms (Table 3 ). This subsection summarises details of the RL algorithm and includes four subgroups: a) MDP type, b) the type of learning, b) the type of policy update, and c) the type of exploration. MDP type specifies MDP model and includes the following abbreviations: NS - nonstationary, ep - episodic, seq - sequential. The type of learning specifies whether the algorithm is model-based (model-based) or model-free (model-free).
